Anchor sets are mixed: 39 items use a 5-level difficulty run, 12 are binary, and 5 are 6 wide against 5 live levels. For those 5 the respondent count identifies the missing category: PFC1-PFC5 run n=1069, 1494, 2133, 1799 and 2145 against a 2535 median for the other 51 items, and the deficit tracks item easiness (Spearman -0.8; PFC1, 'open a previously opened jar', pairs the largest deficit, n=1069, with the highest mean resp, 4.48). Dropping the top 'Very easy' category produces exactly that pattern, so levels 1-5 map onto keys 1-5 (Impossible..Easy). The 26th cross-checked item, PFC43, differs by one word: the codebook prints 'able to do use your hands' where the instrument prints 'able to use your hands', a dittography in the codebook, and the codebook wording ships verbatim as the study's own document.

The codebook names each of CESD1-CESD20 and pairs it with its own stem and its four numbered options, so every item is tied to its text by a label match, not an order inference, and all 20 share one response set. Independent of the codebook, the data confirm the tie at four positions: the canonical CES-D words items 4, 8, 12 and 16 positively, the shipped stems put the positive wording at exactly those numbers, and those four are the only items correlating negatively with the rest -- mean r against the other 19 of -0.293, -0.187, -0.277 and -0.293 against +0.224 to +0.339 for all sixteen others, with no overlap. validate_items.R reports item-set and resp-set matching live data (20 items, 15,471 rows).

The codebook names each of the 24 codes and pairs it with its own stem and numbered options, so every item is tied to its text by a label match rather than an order inference; 20 items carry the 0-3 difficulty run and 4 carry the yes/no aids run, and all 87 shipped option cells re-derive from the codebook. validate_items.R reports item-set and resp-set matching live data (24 items, 37,677 rows). Corroboration rather than a second pin: items sharing a numeric prefix, i.e. the instrument's activity category, cohere more than items across two categories, within-category mean r=0.582 over 16 pairs against 0.499 over 174 -- the predicted direction, with overlapping ranges because the HAQ index is strongly unidimensional.

The block lists exactly 7 sources and the table has exactly 7 items, and all 7 codes are columns of Final_COVIDiSTRESS_Vol2_cleaned.csv. The ladder is read off the administered form, and every live level 1-10 maps onto one of its positions with none left over, which is what the workbooks' 1-7 design could not do. What the form does not settle is which of the 7 codes is which source beyond listing order.

The 6 misperception items are pinned individually by the B.1.1-B.3.2 numbering against codes misperception1_1-misperception3_2. The form's stated randomisation is visible in the data and confirms that structure: it shows one statement per B block, and those 6 items average n=6,561 against 13,069 for the other 7, a ratio of 0.502. The remaining 7 items rest on listing order with counts agreeing at 4 and 3. All 13 codes are columns of the cleaned file, and every live level 1-7 maps onto the administered ladder.

The administered form lists exactly 6 resilience and 5 uncertainty statements against codes resilience_1-6 and uncertainty_1-5, and all 11 codes are columns of the cleaned file. The two blocks' distinct ladders are independently corroborated by the data: resilience items use levels 1-7 and uncertainty items only 1-5, matching the 7-point agreement and 5-point characteristic ladders the form prints for them. Within each block the tie rests on listing order.

The block lists exactly 4 statements and the table has exactly 4 items, all of them columns of the cleaned file, and the wording agrees word for word across both workbooks and the administered form. The 0-6 coding is settled by cross-tabulating each item's _0neutral and _midneutral copies, which gives 0->4, 1->1, 2->2, 3->3, 4->5, 5->6, 6->7 for all four, so 0 is the ladder's Neutral midpoint. What is not settled beyond listing order is which of the 4 codes is which statement.

The block lists exactly 11 statements against codes moral.values_1-11_0neutral, all columns of the cleaned file. The 0-6 coding is settled by cross-tabulating each item's _0neutral and _midneutral copies, which gives 0->4, 1->1, 2->2, 3->3, 4->5, 5->6, 6->7 for all eleven, so 0 is the ladder's Neutral midpoint rather than its floor. The tie between a given code and a given statement rests on listing order.

The three blocks are pinned by the table's own item_family column (1/2/3, 8 items each) together with the instrument's per-block wording. Position 7 is pinned by a response fingerprint: it is the single reverse-worded behaviour and index 7 is the outlier in all three blocks, mean r against block-mates -0.09, +0.11 and -0.04 against +0.25 to +0.60 elsewhere. Block sizes are confirmed by the stated randomisation, each participant receiving 2 of the 8 norm behaviours, visible as norm blocks averaging n=3,794 and n=3,777 against n=15,081 for compliance over 15,607 respondents, a ratio of 0.251. Every live level 1-7 maps onto the administered ladder. The other 7 positions within each block rest on listing order.

The 10 PSS items appear in the instrument in their canonical order against codes perceived_stress_sca_1-10, and the 4 primary stressors likewise; all 28 codes are columns of the cleaned file and every live level 0-4 maps onto the administered ladder. The 14 secondary stressors are ordered as the administered form prints them, which differs from the workbooks, and that order fits the conditional-block respondent counts at 12 of 14 positions: 1-4 general at about 10,000, 5 relationship at 6,607, 6-7 occupation at 9,905 and 9,623, 10-11 student at 1,174 and 1,106, 12-13 children at 3,325 and 3,112, 14 others at 8,359. Indices 8 and 9 carry 6 and 8 responses against about 9,700 for their block-mates, which no ordering explains and which is therefore treated as a source display defect.

The willingness item is tied to vaccine_0neutral unambiguously, being the only item in its block, and its 0-4 coding is settled by cross-tabulating its _0neutral and _midneutral copies, which gives 0->3, 1->1, 2->2, 3->4, 4->5, so 0 is the 5-point ladder's midpoint. The administered form lists exactly 6 attitude statements and the data carry exactly 6 attitude codes, all columns of the cleaned file, with every live level 0-6 mapping onto the agreement ladder. But those codes are numbered 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9, so the match of ascending code order to printed order is an order inference over a numbering with gaps.
